title: Vortex Mixer

references.label: General microbiology laboratory manuals (ASM curriculum resources)

purpose: A benchtop instrument that rapidly agitates the contents of a tube or vial in an orbital motion, used to resuspend pellets, mix reagents, and homogenize samples before pipetting.
operatingPrinciple: A motor drives an off-center cup or platform in a small, fast circular motion; pressing a tube against the cup (or resting it on a touch-activated platform) transfers that motion to the liquid inside, creating a turbulent vortex that mixes the contents.
basicOperation: Ensure the tube cap is secure before mixing.
For a touch-activated unit, press the tube firmly against the cup at an angle to engage mixing; for a continuous unit, place the tube in a holder or against the platform.
Mix for the duration and speed appropriate to the task — brief pulses for gentle resuspension, longer runs for stubborn pellets or thorough mixing.
Check that the liquid does not splash into the cap threads or out of the tube, especially with small volumes.
importantSettings: Speed setting (some units are variable-speed; higher speed increases mixing intensity but also splash risk in small tubes)
maintenance: Wipe down the cup/platform periodically to remove spilled material.
Check that the unit sits stably on the bench and does not 'walk' during operation.

commonErrors.problem: Sample splashes into the cap or out of the tube
commonErrors.cause: Speed set too high for the tube fill volume, or cap not fully secured
commonErrors.fix: Reduce speed, use shorter pulses, and confirm the cap is properly closed

commonErrors.cause: Insufficient mixing time/speed, or pellet adhered too firmly to the tube wall
commonErrors.fix: Increase mixing time, use a higher speed setting, or briefly pipette up-and-down in addition to vortexing

safety: Ensure tube caps are fully closed before vortexing biological or hazardous material to prevent aerosol release.
Avoid vortexing samples known to be sensitive to shear stress (some cell suspensions) without confirming this is appropriate for the task.
